name: Heatless Desiccant Air Dryers
title: Desiccant Air Dryers, 300–2000 CFM | Win Equipments
description: WHD heatless desiccant compressor air dryers, 300–2000 CFM, −20 °C to −40 °C pressure dew point. Win Equipments, Coimbatore.
card: Twin-tower dryers that adsorb moisture for −20 °C to −40 °C pressure dew points.
lede: Where a +3 °C dew point is not dry enough, WHD heatless dryers pass compressed air through a bed of activated alumina or molecular sieve. One tower dries while the other regenerates with a small flow of purge air, switching every few minutes.

price.detail: Compact wall-mounted 10–40 CFM: ₹15,000. Heatless 20–1000 CFM: from ₹1,20,000. 121–500 CFM: ₹2,50,000.

highlights: Pressure relief valves on both towers
Shipped fully assembled, piped and wired

principle.intro: A heatless desiccant dryer removes water vapour by adsorption onto a desiccant bed. No heater is used: a small part of the dried air regenerates the off-line tower.

stages.name: Pre-filter
stages.text: A pre-filter removes free water, oil and dust scale that would damage the desiccant.

stages.name: Adsorb
stages.text: Wet air flows up through the on-line tower; the desiccant bed adsorbs water vapour. Low velocities stop bed fluidisation and dusting.

stages.name: Purge
stages.text: A small flow of dry air is expanded through the off-line tower and exhausted through a muffler, stripping the moisture it holds.

stages.name: Switch
stages.text: The timer and solenoid valves switch towers on a fixed cycle so one tower is always drying.

stages.name: After-filter
stages.text: An after-filter removes desiccant dust before the air reaches your equipment.

spec.caption: WHD series technical specifications
notes: A: activated alumina, pressure dew point −20 °C at 38 °C and 7 bar g working pressure.
M: molecular sieves, pressure dew point −40 °C at 38 °C and 7 bar g working pressure.
Design pressure 13.2 bar g. Standard supply 220 V AC ± 5%, 1 Ph, 50 Hz.
Model code: WHD + capacity code (e.g. WHD 100 = 1000 CFM) + desiccant type.

filters_note: Every dryer should have a pre-filter (free water and dust), a zero-oil filter (oil carried over from the compressor shortens desiccant life) and an after-filter (desiccant dust).
applications: Outdoor air lines in cold conditions
applications_note: Typical uses for sub-zero dew points; confirm suitability for your process with our engineers.

faqs.q: Alumina or molecular sieve: which do I need?
faqs.a: Activated alumina gives a −20 °C pressure dew point; molecular sieve gives −40 °C (both at 38 °C inlet and 7 bar g). Choose molecular sieve when your process needs the lower dew point.

faqs.q: Why does a desiccant dryer need filters?
faqs.a: A pre-filter keeps free water and dust off the desiccant, a zero-oil filter stops compressor oil from coating it, and an after-filter catches desiccant dust before it reaches your equipment.
The off-line tower is regenerated with a small flow of dry purge air instead of a heater, so there is no heater to maintain.
Standard WHD dryers work from 7 to 12.5 bar g with a design pressure of 13.2 bar g. Higher pressures can be offered on request.

air_line.heading: Complete the air line
air_line.text: A heatless desiccant dryer does its job best when the air arrives already cooled and drained. An aftercooler removes most of the water first, so the desiccant bed has less moisture to take up. Automatic drain valves clear condensate from the receiver and filters ahead of the dryer.
